easy.q: What name did Elder Chigbundu give to the strength that helps us withstand the challenges of life?
options: Spiritual immunity
Spiritual sunshine
Spiritual harvest
easy.why: He said that during the health crisis he reflected on what he calls “spiritual immunity,” which gives us strength and courage to withstand life’s challenges.

easy.q: Where did Elder Chigbundu keep hearing the word “immunity” in 2020?
options: On a visit to a family doctor
In health sessions at his work
In a science class at school
easy.why: Leaders at his workplace invited health professionals to teach about COVID-19, and in those sessions “there was one recurring word: immunity.”

easy.q: A new missionary cried and asked to be sent home. What did Elder Chigbundu, his mission leader, encourage him to do?
options: Write to his family every week
Move to a different area
Study the Book of Mormon
easy.why: He bore testimony of the Book of Mormon and encouraged the missionary to study the scriptures. Later the missionary wrote, “I am happy now and do not want to be sent home any longer.”

easy.q: Elder Chigbundu visited a sister who was very sick. What did she say she realizes as she prays each day?
options: That the Savior loves her
That she will be well soon
That she should move away
easy.why: She told him, “As I pray daily, I realize that the Savior loves me.” She felt Him telling her that all is well.

easy.q: Which four “small and simple things” did Elder Chigbundu invite us to always remember?
options: Fasting, tithing, service, and family history
Scriptures, prayers, the sacrament, and covenants
Hymns, journals, missions, and Church meetings
easy.why: Near the end he said, “I invite you to always remember scriptures, prayers, the sacrament, and covenants.” These were the four things his talk was built around.

medium.q: In words Elder Chigbundu quoted from President Henry B. Eyring, proving moments are evidence of what?
options: That the Lord has stepped back to let us grow alone
That we have wandered from the covenant path
That the Lord loves us enough to refine and strengthen us
That life’s troubles come mostly by chance
medium.why: President Eyring said such moments are not evidence that the Lord has abandoned us; “they are evidence that He loves you enough to refine and strengthen you.”

medium.q: Elder Chigbundu said the Lord has given us “a spiritual compass” to help us navigate life’s challenges. What did he say that compass is?
options: Small and simple things
Great and dramatic miracles
Our own best judgment
The example of people around us
medium.why: He named the compass “small and simple things” and quoted Alma: “By small and simple things are great things brought to pass.”

medium.q: What does the story of the new missionary who asked to go home best show?
options: That homesickness fades by itself if we simply wait
That a struggling missionary needs a new companion
That a leader’s testimony can stand in for our own
That daily scripture study can change how we see our purpose
medium.why: The missionary later testified that daily scripture study had helped him understand his purpose as a missionary, and he no longer wanted to be sent home.

medium.q: According to Elder Chigbundu, what happens to the burdens we carry as we pray in faith?
options: They are always taken away once our faith is strong enough
They may remain, but our backs will be built to carry them
They are passed to others who are stronger than we are
They stay the same until we stop thinking about them
medium.why: He taught, “The burden we carry may not always be removed, but our backs will be built to carry the load placed upon them.”

medium.q: Elder Chigbundu said that as we remember Jesus Christ through the week, our “Why me?” questions will be replaced. By what?
options: Asking when our trials will finally come to an end
Asking who is to blame for what has gone wrong
Asking what others should be doing to help us
Asking what we can learn and what we can change
medium.why: He said our “Why me?” questions will be replaced by “What can I learn, and what can I change?” as our lives are gradually refined and reshaped.

hard.q: Elder Chigbundu named two fruits of scripture study and said how the Lord’s words come to shape us. Which summary is faithful to what he taught?
options: Knowledge matters most, and it shapes us as we read more widely
Knowing the Lord matters most, and His words shape us once memorized
Knowing the Lord matters most, and His words shape us as we apply them
Knowledge and knowing the Lord are one thing, gained by reading daily
hard.why: He said “we get knowledge, but more important, we come to know the Lord,” and that it is “as we apply what we learn” that His words begin to shape how we think and respond.

hard.q: Which situation best fits what Elder Chigbundu taught about prayer and our burdens?
options: A man prays once about a trial and, when it stays, decides prayer has failed
A family prays hard in a crisis, then stops once the crisis has passed
A woman prays daily; her illness remains, but she feels strength and the Savior’s love
A youth waits to pray until his problem is small enough to handle alone
hard.why: He taught that the burden “may not always be removed,” but as we pray in faith we are strengthened to carry it, as the sister he visited had found.

hard.q: How did Elder Chigbundu describe the link between making covenants and staying on the covenant path?
options: Making covenants brings every blessing; the path is only for those who stumble
Covenants create a bond with God; staying on the path brings its promised blessings
Staying on the path comes first; covenants are the reward given at the end
Either one, kept faithfully without the other, secures the promised blessings
hard.why: He called them “inseparable companions”: covenants create a bond between us and God, and staying on the covenant path brings the promised blessings that come with that bond.

hard.q: According to Elder Chigbundu, what do we receive as we worship in the temple and remember our covenants, even though trials may come?
options: A promise that our trials will be brief
Knowledge that makes daily prayer less needed
Blessings that no longer depend on obedience
Personal direction from the Lord for our path
hard.why: He said that “we receive personal direction from the Lord that will guide us along the covenant path.” The promise is guidance through trials, not freedom from them.

hard.q: The talk opens with immunity and closes by calling four small and simple things “the armor of God.” What do the two pictures share in Elder Chigbundu’s teaching?
options: Both are a protection that helps us stand when challenges come
Both are a cure that takes our trials away once fully received
Both are a gift given once that needs no further effort from us
Both are a strength kept for those who hold special callings
hard.why: Immunity defends and protects; spiritual immunity gives strength “to withstand the challenges of life.” Likewise these four things are “truly the armor of God” that helps us stand, not an escape from trials.
